messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: increase in 5xx rate from gateway (prod us-east-1). Alert id: PD-2100. See https://ops.redwood/alerts/PD-2100

sara (oncall): on it, paging into #incidents. first look: is this correlated with deploys?

ken: no deploys in the last 2 hours. I'm seeing a cascade: clients hitting rate limits -> many 429s, then retry storms causing backend queue exhaust -> 5xx from our model gateway.

maya: confirming logs show spike in 429s at 08:12:03 UTC, then 502/503 from model-proxy after 08:12:18. attaching small snippet of aggregated logs:

```
rate_limiter: client_id=cli-77 limit=120/s returned=429 count=4321 window=1s
model-proxy: upstream_timeout service=model-worker-3 latency=1.2s returns=502
```

devon: could be quota misapply on our global policy. I see a recent policy push to tighten default concurrency for burst protection (policy id: qp-2026-tight). Might be too aggressive for some clients.

sara (oncall): model tier fallback is enabled? we should switch overloaded clients to lower-cost variant to reduce load while we investigate.

ken: yes fallback exists but it's gated by the rate-limiter. We should: 1) temporarily relax the global per-second quota to allow queued requests to drain OR 2) enable immediate model-variant fallback before 429. Which is faster?

maya: temporary quota tweak is fastest. I can patch the rate-limit config to raise default from 120/s -> 300/s for 5m for affected pools. Patch command: `rbctl rate-limit update --policy qp-2026-tight --set default_rps=300 --duration 5m`

devon: also recommend enabling request-level jittered backoff at the gateway so we avoid synchronized retries -> add header `Retry-After` with increasing backoff for clients that hit 429.

sara (oncall): proceed with Maya's patch, but keep an eye on model-proxy CPU and queue depth. If model-proxy saturates, we'll flip to variant fallback + circuit-breaker.

maya: applying patch now. Output:

```
$ rbctl rate-limit update --policy qp-2026-tight --set default_rps=300 --duration 5m
policy qp-2026-tight updated -> default_rps=300 (temp 5m)
```

maya: patch applied. monitoring…

raj: adding quick dashboard links: rate-limiter QPS https://dash.redwood/rate/qps, model-proxy queue https://dash.redwood/queue/model-proxy.

support-bot: Noted: increased 5xx from 08:12 -> 08:24. Customer-impact: several API keys show degraded success rates. Logged cases: 3 enterprise customers opened support tickets.

ken: initial metrics: 5xx rate peaked at 3.8% of requests (baseline 0.05%). Concurrent model-proxy queue length hit 480 requests (safe limit 200).

sara (oncall): queue at 480 -> pushing model-proxy into overload. Need immediate mitigations: 1) enable model-variant fallback for requests from non-SLA customers; 2) enforce stricter per-client burst caps for repeat offenders; 3) throttle heavy clients with 429 but include `Retry-After`.

devon: I'll roll out a traffic-split rule to divert 30% of new incoming traffic to a smaller-CPU model variant (variant v2-small) for 20 minutes. Command: `rbctl traffic-split set --route /generate --variant v2-small:30% --duration 20m`

maya: traffic-split rolled out. Monitoring latency and token generation errors.

support-bot: Sent automated notice to account teams for the 3 impacted enterprise customers: AcmeHealth, Ledgerly, and NeoRetail. Notifying account owners for potential SLA impact.

ken: model-proxy queue dropping slowly after both patch and split. current queue 210. 5xx down to 1.1% and trending.

maya: also enabled circuit-breaker on model-proxy upstream to fail fast for overloaded workers: `rbctl proxy cb enable model-proxy --threshold 300 --cooldown 30s`

devon: observing drop in retry storm after circuit-breaker enable. Good. We should still root cause: why did qp-2026-tight apply broadly?

sara (oncall): agree. I want a postmortem but first handoff to night oncall. Emily, can you take next 2 hours, watch for regression, and own the follow-up? Summary for handoff below.

emily (next-oncall): taking over. Quick questions: are any customer throttles permanent changes?

maya: No permanent changes. Rate-limit bump is temporary 5m expired at 08:17, but we also applied traffic-split and circuit-breaker which remain for 20m and 30s respectively. I'll schedule automatic rollback at expiry.

raj: add a temp monitoring alert: if model-proxy queue > 250 -> pg oncall. I'll push now.

support-bot: Support update sent: initial triage in #incidents, mitigation applied (rate-limit bump, traffic-split, circuit-breaker). ETA for stability: 20m.

emily (next-oncall): thanks. I'll keep an eye and start a deeper investigation into policy rollout history for qp-2026-tight. Who owns that policy?

devon: policy authored by infra-policy-team (owner: @ken). There's a PR merged this morning that tightened defaults; looks like the rollout included global scope accidentally instead of region-limited.

ken: ack. That's my mistake — I mis-scoped the rollout. I'll open an emergency revert PR and coordinate safer rollout steps.

sara (oncall): thanks, Ken. For the handoff notes, please include: timeline, commands executed, metrics at peak, customers impacted, and follow-up action items for postmortem (policy rollback, adding automated canary for rate-limit changes, and runbook update).

emily (next-oncall): logging handoff: taking ownership at 08:30 UTC. Current status: 5xx at 0.4%, queue 95, traffic-split active (v2-small 30%), circuit-breaker enabled. Will watch for 1 hour and coordinate with infra-policy-team for rollback PR.

devon: I'll draft the postmortem starter and link timeline so we can track RCA.

maya: note for later: add unit/regression tests to the policy rollout job to catch global vs region scoping.

support-bot: Customer follow-up: account teams notified, tickets flagged P2, suggested credit for impacted windows once final scope of impact known.

sara (oncall): closing pager for now. If anything spikes back above queue 250 or 5xx > 1.5% reopen. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

emily (next-oncall): continuing monitoring. I'll update this thread with any regressions or the final postmortem link.

incident-bot: Incident PD-2100 status -> mitigated (initial). Follow-up tasks created: TASK-3312 (policy revert), TASK-3313 (postmortem), TASK-3314 (runbook updates).

emily (next-oncall): noted. ending handoff at 08:45 UTC.
